heading: Computer Science Fundamentals
subheading: Core concepts in algorithms, data structures, and computing

items.question: What is the difference between a Stack and a Queue?
items.answer: A Stack follows the Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) principle, where elements are added and removed from the top. A Queue follows First-In, First-Out (FIFO), where elements enter at the rear and exit from the front.

items.question: What is Big-O notation?
items.answer: Big-O notation describes the upper bound of an algorithm's runtime or space requirements as the input size grows toward infinity. For example, O(1) is constant time, O(n) is linear time, and O(log n) is logarithmic time.

items.question: How does binary search achieve O(log n) time complexity?
items.answer: Binary search requires a sorted array. At each step, it compares the target with the median element, effectively dividing the remaining search space by half until the target is found or bounds cross.

items.question: What is idempotency in API design?
items.answer: An idempotent operation produces the same result no matter how many times it is executed. For example, HTTP GET, PUT, and DELETE are idempotent, whereas POST is typically non-idempotent.
